_comment: Generated by scripts/conformance_scoreboard.py — per-policy conformance drill-down for one jurisdiction. Do not hand-edit.

policies.note: The us-aca-ptc-grid suite compares six full-year 2026 IRC 36B cases. It binds PE-US used_aca_ptc rather than raw aca_ptc so the compared boundary includes the enrolled-plan premium cap present in Axiom. The committed report is 6/6 within one cent and includes nonzero cases.

Lapsed before the 2026 validation year: the Affordable Connectivity Program (47 USC 1752; IIJA 2021 sec. 60502) stopped new enrollments 2024-02-07 and paid its last partial benefit for May 2024 as appropriated funds were exhausted. PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 zeroes gov.fcc.acp.amount for 2026, so acp pays 0 for every synthetic case even with is_acp_eligible forced on and broadband_cost 2400 (probe evidence: scripts/probe_us_repealed_federal.py). Axiom encodes current law and has no current-law ACP surface to compare.

The us-additional-medicare-grid suite compares PE-US additional_medicare_tax with Axiom's combined final only on the explicitly bounded tax-year-2026 zero-self-employment domain: five wage-only GRID-CONTRACT cases across single, joint, and married-filing-separately status, four nonzero. For zero-SE inputs, PE-US additional_medicare_tax equals the section 3101(b)(2) wage-only amount and Axiom's combined output remains valid. The suite does not test or claim the section 1401(b)(2) self-employment leg; SE leg pending the 26 CFR 1.1401-1 operative-authority chain, axiom-corpus#523. The committed report is 5/5 within one cent.

The al-income-tax-populace evidence compares only the canonical section 40-18-5 schedule-before-credits output to al_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits after validated projection of completed al_taxable_income and schedule status. It does not prove final annual al_income_tax.
Covered by al-tanf-ecps — Alabama Family Assistance (al_tanf) vs PE-2026 at population scale after requested-month regeneration (1441/1444 match, 3 unexplained).
Covered by fiit-ecps (us:tax/federal-income-tax#aotc).

The state-tax Populace campaign validates the narrower Arkansas Act 2 individual schedule component ar_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits_indiv at Person grain and sums both sides to TaxUnit only for accounting. The reviewed RuleSpec does not expose broad final ar_income_tax or the former six-case liability-grid output, so that stale grid suite has been retired and broad ar_income_tax remains uncovered.

The az-income-tax-liability grid and full-Populace campaign validate only az_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits. Final az_income_tax also applies charitable-contribution, dependent, family, increased-excise-tax, and property-tax credits; 499 of 1,585 routed units differ from the narrow target.
Covered by az-tanf-ecps — Arizona Cash Assistance (az_tanf) vs PE-2026 at population scale.

Reform lever, not a baseline statutory program: basic_income is $0 in the baseline and only set by a UBI reform. PE computes it, but there is no enacted statute to conform against — reform scaffolding.

The ca-income-tax-liability suite is a six-case ordinary resident single/joint grid against ca_income_tax_before_refundable_credits. It does not cover refundable credits, and its RuleSpec slice also excludes the high-rate, head-of-household, AMT, and mental-health-tax branches, so it does not establish final ca_income_tax liability.
Covered by ca-tanf-ecps — CalWORKs (ca_tanf) vs PE-2026 at population scale; residuals undispositioned.
Covered by fiit-ecps (us:tax/federal-income-tax#capital_gain).
Covered by fiit-ecps (us:tax/federal-income-tax#cdcc).
Reported income carried from the CPS (no formula); PE-US carries it into net income but computes no award from statute — a carried input, not a simulated program.

PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 imputes this annual Person value as state separate-CHIP spending divided by enrollment, using calibration.gov.hhs.cms.chip.spending.separate_chip.total[state_code] and calibration.gov.hhs.cms.chip.enrollment.separate_chip[state_code], then gates it on chip_enrolled (eligibility plus take-up). This is a per-capita expenditure imputation, not a statutory amount formula; is_chip_eligible is compared separately.

In-scope uncovered — the reviewed Colorado Populace comparison validates only the C.R.S. section 39-22-104(1.7)(c) base tax on completed-return Colorado taxable income. Section 39-22-627 temporary rate adjustments and credits needed for final co_income_tax remain outside that suite.
Covered by co-tanf-ecps — Colorado Works (co_tanf) vs PE-2026 at population scale.

PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 imputes this annual Person value directly from gov.usda.csfp.amount, an administrative cost-per-participant parameter derived from program cost divided by participation, and gates it on commodity_supplemental_food_program_eligible. This is a food-package/caseload service-value imputation, not a statutory amount formula; commodity_supplemental_food_program_eligible is compared separately (rulespec-us PR #1008).

The ct-income-tax-populace campaign validates only the canonical full-year-resident ordinary section 12-700 tax before the personal credit, recovered exactly from ct_income_tax_after_personal_credits and ct_personal_credit_rate. It does not claim the personal credit, alternative minimum tax, property-tax or stillborn credits, refundable ct_eitc, payments, refunds, or final ct_income_tax.
Covered by fiit-ecps (us:tax/federal-income-tax#ctc).

The dc-income-tax-liability suite is a six-case ordinary resident wage-earner grid against dc_income_tax_before_credits. It does not cover nonrefundable or refundable credits or establish the full-population filing-method branches required for final dc_income_tax liability.

Covered by de-tanf-ecps — Delaware TANF (de_tanf) vs PE-2026 at population scale (781/781 match, 0 unexplained).

This is an administrative slot-cost imputation, not a statutory amount formula; is_early_head_start_eligible is compared separately (rulespec-us PR #1010).

The us-itemized-taxable-income-deductions-grid suite compares 17 engine-verified 2026 RuleSpec companion cases (16 nonzero) across all five filing statuses with PE-US 1.767.3 under PolicyEngine 4.18.9 and Core 3.30.3. It binds the same six completed post-entitlement, post-limitation components and keeps the completed lawful taxable-income-without-section-68 scalar RuleSpec-only because PE derives a non-equivalent AGI-minus-exemptions proxy. This aggregate-only boundary does not certify component entitlement, substantiation, components outside PE's six-item inventory, miscellaneous deductions above zero, or the section 63(e) itemization election. The section 68 wrong-base and truncated-rate cases remain visible as source divergences carried only by evidence-backed per-case dispositions; their upstream issues are itemized-68-other-deduction-base=policyengine-us#9170 and itemized-68-rational-rate=policyengine-us#9171. Suite coverage does not assert raw equality on those cases.

There is no current-law Chapter 77 tax instrument to compare; the RuleSpec repeal-result module records that legal absence rather than an operative zero-rate schedule.

The us-salt-deduction-grid suite compares 16 nonzero, engine-verified 2026 RuleSpec companion cases across all five filing statuses with PE-US 1.767.3 under PolicyEngine 4.18.9 and Core 3.30.3. It binds completed elected personal income-or-sales tax and real-estate tax directly and bridges the guarded section 911 amount to PE-US foreign_earned_income_exclusion. The completed-return boundary excludes business and section 212 taxes, acquisition-capitalized taxes, refunds, nondeductible taxes, state-liability synthesis, and any unlisted section 911 individual; personal-property tax remains RuleSpec-only. The low-AGI simulation ceiling, omitted personal-property-tax source, and AGI-instead-of-statutory-MAGI cases remain visible as source divergences carried only by evidence-backed per-case dispositions. Their upstream issues are salt-low-agi-engine-cap=policyengine-us#9167, salt-magi-911-addback=policyengine-us#9168, and salt-personal-property-tax-probe=policyengine-us#9169. Suite coverage does not assert raw equality on those cases.

The us-savers-grid suite compares Axiom's pre-section-26 section 25B amount with its reviewed direct PE-US target, savers_credit_potential, on 34 fixture-bound tax-year-2026 cases. It does not compare PE's liability-limited public credit. The grid covers all five filing statuses, every exact Notice 2025-67 tier ceiling plus B-1 and B+1, per-person contribution caps, the section 25B(e) section 911 add-back, and the age/student/dependent screens. The raw report is 23/34. All 11 differences remain the exact-ceiling cases explained by https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/issues/9151: PE-US 1.767.3 carries the correct values, but Core 3.30.3 digitizes equality into the next tier despite section 25B(b)'s inclusive ceilings. The dispositioned report is 100% explained. The section 911 case's observed match is cancellation between PE's omitted add-back and #9151, not evidence of add-back parity.

Both boundaries include OASDI plus ordinary Medicare and exclude the separate 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax; the committed report is 6/6 with nonzero cases.

SNAP is one national PE-US variable (snap). Covered by ca-snap-ecps, the largest of 11 state-scoped SNAP suites validating the same snap surface vs PE-2026. The ten month-scoped suites regenerated on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3 retain AL/AZ/CA/FL/GA/MA/NC/NY/SC/TN unexplained counts of 40/0/241/774/75/92/49/240/110/43 after evidence-backed dispositions. For CA, PUB 275 issuance or online access is a household administrative fact absent from Enhanced CPS; both facts remain unmapped, and neither the population encode nor the oracle assumes them, leaving 157 bridge-attributed residual rows. Resolving them requires a population source carrying household PUB 275 issuance/access or PolicyEngine modeling the same household gate. PolicyEngine-US issues https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/issues/9175 and https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/issues/9176 remain independently verified divergences on the pinned stack, but the corrected bridge cannot currently expose them because the household MCE gate is unobserved. The row registers the canonical largest-population suite; the other ten corroborate and their residuals remain tracked — the scoreboard scores one suite per row, not silently dropped.

PE-US sums reported OASDI benefit components (retirement, disability, dependents, survivors) carried from the CPS; it computes no Title II entitlement from earnings history, so there is no simulated statutory surface to compare — a reported passthrough.

Technical SPM resource-accounting construct, not a statutory housing benefit: PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 computes min(housing_assistance, max(spm_unit_spm_threshold_housing_portion - hud_ttp, 0)). The housing-assistance and tenant-payment operands are modeled HUD amounts, but the outer cap comes from Census SPM thresholds, tenure housing shares, and geographic adjustment rather than a statutory payment parameter; forcing housing_assistance 30000, the SPM housing portion 17720, and hud_ttp 10000 returns 7720 (probe evidence: scripts/probe_us_ira_2026.py). Validate Section 8 or HAP against hud_hap, or against housing_assistance with take-up pinned, and exclude this SPM post-processing row as technical.

The wa-income-tax-liability suite is a six-case RCW 82.87 capital-gains grid against wa_income_tax_before_refundable_credits. It excludes refundable credits and does not certify the full-population asset-sourcing and loss-carryforward surface, so it does not establish final wa_income_tax.
Covered by wa-tanf-ecps — Washington TANF (wa_tanf) vs PE-2026 at population scale.

The wi-income-tax-liability suite is a six-case ordinary resident wage-earner schedule grid against wi_income_tax_before_credits. It excludes credits and the retirement-income-exclusion alternative, and the pinned oracle has stale or unrounded 2026 brackets, so it does not establish final wi_income_tax.

PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 imputes this monthly Person value from the average food-package parameter gov.usda.wic.value[wic_food_package_str], adjusted with gov.usda.wic.cvb.current, gov.usda.wic.cvb.included_in_value, and gov.usda.wic.cvb.replaces_included_value, then gates it on is_wic_eligible and would_claim_wic (subject to gov.usda.wic.abolish_wic). This is a package-value imputation, not a statutory amount formula; is_wic_eligible is compared separately (rulespec-us PR #1010).
Reported income carried from the CPS (no formula); PE-US carries it into net income but computes no award from statute — a carried input, not a simulated program.

The wv-income-tax-liability grid and full-Populace campaign validate only wv_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits. Final wv_income_tax additionally applies low-income-family and CDCC credits plus refundable state-CTC and homestead-excess-property-tax credits; 217 of 1,608 routed units differ from the narrow target.
